ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a schematic diagram of the Earth’s graticule represented by a circle. Inside the outer circle there are multiple radial meridians and dashed latitude circles; there is a relatively thick curve in the figure representing the terminator line, and the stem states that this terminator line is tangent to the polar circle at point P. The figure also marks point P, point A above, and the 180° meridian label at the lower left. Reasoning: London is located in the 0 time zone, and Beijing uses East Eighth Zone time; at this time London is still Saturday while Beijing is already Sunday, indicating that Beijing enters the new day earlier than London, and from this the position of the 0 o’clock meridian in the figure can be judged. Combining this with the fact that point P is the tangent point between the terminator line and the polar circle, as well as the local-time relationship near point P and the 180° meridian, it can be determined that this solar term corresponds to the Northern Hemisphere summer solstice, not the winter solstice. Around the Northern Hemisphere summer solstice is approximately late June, and in normal years the Jianghuai region at this time enters the seasonal precipitation period formed under the influence of a quasi-stationary front, namely the plum rain period.

The figure also marks point P, point A above, and the 180° meridian label at the lower left. Combining this with the fact that point P is the tangent point between the terminator line and the polar circle, as well as the local-time relationship near point P and the 180° meridian, it can be determined that this solar term corresponds to the Northern Hemisphere summer solstice, not the winter solstice.
